issue.title: Cover identical-lexical duplicate redistribution in UPDATE comparison
issue.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

Track the missing identical-lexical duplicate-redistribution case raised in [PR #6482's Copilot review](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/pull/6482#discussion_r3980166727).

In `crates/sparq-bench/src/update_fuzz.rs`, `comparable()` canonicalizes blank-node snapshots as sets. When the canonical vectors compare equal, `compare()` checks only total raw row counts before returning `Same`. This path is byte-identical between main `4595388de9e389f5369d63828fbf90cfc16b62d9` and PR head `fe3284199db0831f353d2ae401b8c69472764904`.

The existing new test covers different lexical forms (`020/021` on one side and `20/21` on the other). It reaches lexical adjudication and passed in the frozen Rust 2021 suite. It does not cover otherwise identical spellings with redistributed duplicates.

Minimal next witness: let `p` and `q` be distinct complete quads sharing blank-node subject `_:x`, with integer objects `020` and `021`. Compare `[p,p,q]` against `[p,q,q]`, using exactly the same spellings on both sides. Preserve the current different-spelling test as a control. Source analysis indicates that equal canonical sets plus equal total counts can hide the redistribution; this exact new runtime witness has not yet been executed, so this is not a reported engine failure.

Acceptance:

- Run the exact witness and record the actual verdict before changing code.
- If confirmed, make the complete-quad snapshot/probe comparison reject redistributed duplicate rows before the strict `Same` return; retain sound blank-node handling and distinguish graph-set from arbitrary query-result bag semantics.
- Add a regression and a control that removes the new guard, preserving the lexical-adjudication tests, strict error behavior and existing canonicalization protections.
- Validate in the real Rust 2021 crate and normal protected CI. No engine/parser change or canonicalizer weakening implied.

Related: #5183. Separate from the reference-domain repair in #6482; that PR does not change this strict `Same` path.

comment.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

The exact synthetic witness is now confirmed against the unchanged UPDATE comparison module on main `f50b5049627415a0f8fd1eca6dd3cb9ac5fcd464`.

For complete quads `p` and `q` sharing a blank-node subject, `[p,p,q]` versus `[p,q,q]` returns `Same` when both sides use identical integer spellings, with integer-lexical adjudication both disabled and enabled. Both distinct-spelling controls return `Differs`; the enabled control retains the diagnostic that normalization merges or duplicates rows.

This ran as one focused Rust 2021 test of the actual module with its recorded dependencies: four comparisons, one build/run, no production change. The earlier attempt stopped before compiling because of the disk reserve; it is not counted as an execution. The confirmed path canonicalizes blank-node datasets as sets, then accepts equal total raw counts before reaching lexical adjudication. That strict path predates #6482.

This establishes a comparator diagnostic gap, not a demonstrated engine wrong-answer bug. The repair must respect the complete-quad/probe contract, sound blank-node comparison and the fact that arbitrary SPARQL result bags can legitimately contain duplicate rows. I’m checking those call sites before selecting the smallest correction.
